video.title: You Don’t Need an Online Business to Get Rich

summary: Chris Koerner and co-host Nick riff on offline and 'old-school' businesses: hot tub servicing for Airbnbs and hot tub moving for retailers, concierge prep for lake houses, touchless check-in SaaS for boat/kayak rentals, and buying moat-protected destination rental businesses that charge $95 for a 3-hour inner tube. They discuss a Shopify order-confirmation cold email hack, using a B2B directory (ABA autism clinics) as lead generation for an agency, and The Flower Letters, a $10/month subscription of WWII-era story letters with ~31,000 subscribers (~$310k/month) grown by word of mouth. Spin-off ideas include correspondence chess by mail, interactive AI-written kids' story letters, personalised AI story gift books, a directory of niche wedding services, and a niche white-labelled vibe-coding app. Takeaway: analog, local, and 'zig while others zag' businesses with real-world moats are underrated.

speakers.name: Nick
speakers.description: Chris's friend; hosts the Nickonomics podcast; building One Life Tale

ideas.name: Hot tub servicing for short-term rentals and hot tub moving for retailers
ideas.one_liner: Weekly hot tub maintenance for Airbnb owners plus acting as the delivery/logistics arm for hot tub retailers.
ideas.customer: Short-term rental owners; hot tub retail stores
ideas.problem: STR hot tubs need regular servicing; retailers don't want to be in delivery logistics
ideas.offer: Quick weekly service visits; hot tub moving

pricing.model: Weekly subscription per tub; per move

acquisition_channels.details: Retailers outsource moving; STR owners as recurring clients.

ideas.delivery: Family business with teenage daughters servicing ~25 tubs a day in rural Idaho.

acquisition.how: B2B relationships with STR managers and retailers; local SEO possible.

uk_applicability.notes: UK holiday lets with hot tubs (Lake District, Cornwall) have the same need.

quotes.text: they do 25 hot tubs a day. A day in the middle of nowhere Idaho. They charge
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: between $50 and $100 a week to service these. They were here for 5 minutes.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Lake house concierge prep service
ideas.one_liner: Before wealthy owners arrive, gas and service boats and jet skis, tidy the yard and stock the fridge; strip beds after.
ideas.business_model: Per-visit fee plus cost of goods
ideas.problem: Owners waste the start and end of every trip on prep

acquisition_channels.details: Leave flyers at each lake house.

ideas.delivery: Staff physically prep property and watercraft.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: May take months for owners to visit and see flyers

acquisition.how: Flyers in person; addressed post would be PECR-safe in UK.

uk_applicability.notes: Fewer private lake houses; similar for holiday homes and boat owners.

quotes.text: I think that there's an opportunity for somebody to create a concierge prep service for rich people.
quotes.speaker: Nick

ideas.name: Touchless check-in SaaS for recreational rentals
ideas.one_liner: Vibe-coded app for boat, kayak, ATV and paddle board rental shops: pre-arrival waivers, training videos and check boxes so customers just show up and go.
ideas.customer: Watercraft/outdoor rental businesses at vacation destinations
ideas.problem: Customers spend an hour on waivers and instructions; staff time
ideas.offer: QR-code pre-check-in with waivers and how-to videos, like car rental touchless pickup

acquisition_channels.details: Pitch rental businesses directly at destinations; flyers with QR codes.

acquisition.how: Small local businesses; cold email legal to UK limited companies but many are sole traders (consent needed under PECR).

uk_applicability.notes: UK watersports and bike hire shops exist; seasonal.

quotes.text: You could vibe code something that these boat rental places pay for monthly to help streamline the waiver process, the learning process.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Paddle board with integrated electric pump
ideas.one_liner: Inflatable paddle board that inflates/deflates at the press of a button.

quotes.text: Can someone invent a paddle board that has an integrated electric pump?
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Buy moat-protected destination rental businesses
ideas.one_liner: Acquire boomer-owned rental businesses with prime location and domain (Mack's Inn float rentals, BearLakeRentals.com) that charge premium prices.
ideas.offer: Inner tubes, kayaks, paddle boards, canoes, boats

pricing.notes: Comparable inner tube rentals elsewhere about $5/day; tubes cost $15 on Amazon.

unit_economics_claims: $95 inner tube rental vs $15 purchase cost

uk_applicability.notes: UK lake/coast rental businesses exist; seasonality shorter.

quotes.text: $95 to rent an inner tube from Max in $95.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: Imagine buying that boomerowned business, Bearlake Rentals.com, with their own marina right there
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Sign creation and maintenance business
ideas.one_liner: Acquire a durable local sign making/maintenance company (custom and neon signs).

quotes.text: I just talked to a guy who's under LOI for a >> sign printing and maintenance business.

ideas.name: Real-world local business hackathon retreat
ideas.one_liner: Mastermind getaway at a vacation destination where teams compete to launch and earn from an in-person business within a week, filmed as a show.
ideas.offer: Week-long competitive launch retreat with team mentors

acquisition_channels.details: Podcast audience; film as a season.

quotes.text: There are five teams. Whoever can think of and execute the best business model in the next seven days and make the most money wins.
quotes.speaker: Nick

ideas.name: Directory as B2B lead generation for an agency
ideas.one_liner: Build a directory of a vertical's businesses (e.g. ABA autism clinics), cold email the listed businesses, then upsell them premium placement and agency services (PPC, SEO).
ideas.business_model: Premium listings plus agency retainer upsell
ideas.customer: High-LTV, high-trust businesses: healthcare clinics, CPAs, lawyers, restaurants
ideas.problem: Agencies need warm leads; clinics need patients
ideas.offer: Free listing, paid ranking, then agency services

pricing.model: Premium placement and monthly agency retainer (not quantified)

acquisition_channels.details: Email each listed business: you're on my directory, want to rank higher?

unit_economics_claims: Guest gets 90% of his own clinic's leads from a directory
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Takes time to gain SEO traction

acquisition.how: Directory and email sequences automate well; in the UK cold email is legal to limited companies (most clinics, law firms) but sole-trader practitioners need consent under PECR.

delivery.how: Directory is software; agency services agent-assisted.

uk_applicability.notes: Works for UK verticals; healthcare advertising rules (ASA/CAP, CQC) apply.

quotes.text: he's using that as a lead generation source for the clinics, not for patients.
quotes.speaker: Nick

quotes.text: It's a vertically integrated directory to a high ticket monthly recurring offer, right?
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Serialised story-letter subscription (The Flower Letters)
ideas.one_liner: Mail subscribers two 'handwritten' letters a month that tell a WWII-era romance story, with stickers and artwork, for $10/month.
ideas.problem: Desire for a slow, tangible reading experience
ideas.offer: Six storyline series delivered as letters; many subscribe to several

pricing.notes: Some customers pay $20-50/month for multiple series.

acquisition_channels.details: No paid ads per interview; ~60k monthly unique visitors (SimilarWeb).

quote.text: They're not doing paid ads. It's just word of mouth.
quote.speaker: Nick

ideas.delivery: Printed letters mailed via USPS bulk from a warehouse in Orem; started from home.

acquisition.how: Word of mouth, SEO and paid social are inbound.

delivery.how: Story writing can be AI-assisted; printing and mailing outsourced to a print-and-mail fulfilment house.

support.how: AI handles address changes and questions.

uk_applicability.notes: Royal Mail bulk rates are higher than USPS, squeezing margin; otherwise works.

quotes.text: Two letters per month to people paying $10 per month that tell a story.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: A year ago, they had 31,000 active subscribers.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: You don't want to cancel on month three because you don't know how it ends in month 12.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Correspondence chess by mail
ideas.one_liner: Match players at similar ratings for chess games played by letter, with the company forwarding moves or sending kits with pre-stamped envelopes.
ideas.offer: Matched pen-pal chess games by post

acquisition_channels.details: Buy and merge chess Facebook groups.

ideas.delivery: Players submit moves digitally, company mails letters; or kits.

quotes.text: he had a pen pal that he would write letters to and they were in the middle of a chess game.
quotes.speaker: Nick

ideas.name: Interactive AI story letters for kids
ideas.one_liner: Kids receive story letters with prompts, mail back choices, and AI writes the next chapter in a handwritten font; finished story sold as a printed book.
ideas.problem: Kids rarely get real mail; engagement with reading
ideas.offer: Choose-your-own-adventure letters with prepaid return envelopes
ideas.delivery: Mail opened and scanned automatically, uploaded to ChatGPT, response printed and mailed.

delivery.how: Scanning, AI writing and print-and-mail can be automated; mail handling needs a service.

uk_applicability.notes: Children's data (UK GDPR Age Appropriate Design Code) needs care.

quotes.text: It gets put into a machine, gets opened automatically, scanned automatically, uploaded to Chad GPT automatically.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Personalised AI story gift books (One Life Tale)
ideas.one_liner: Relatives answer prompts about a child; AI generates illustrated stories starring the child, printed as gifts.
ideas.customer: Relatives wanting to connect with children
ideas.offer: Monthly prompts producing a personalised story
ideas.delivery: App plus print (e.g. Barnes & Noble print).

quotes.text: I can go and enter information about Carson into this app and it will generate a story for Carson.
quotes.speaker: Nick

ideas.name: Directory of niche wedding services
ideas.one_liner: A long-tail 'The Knot' for quirky wedding vendors (beer burro, 360 photo booths, pizza trucks), monetised later via premium placement.
ideas.business_model: Free listings then paid placement/ads; later marketplace
ideas.customer: Couples planning unique weddings; niche vendors pay
ideas.problem: Hard to find unusual Instagrammable wedding services

acquisition_channels.details: Ads to women about to get married.

ideas.delivery: Scrape vendors, build with Replit; start in one city (e.g. Dallas).
unit_economics_claims: Beer burro donkey rents for $700 a day

uk_applicability.notes: Works for UK weddings; contacting vendors (often sole traders) by cold email needs PECR care; listing scraped data needs GDPR legitimate-interest assessment.

quotes.text: I think someone needs to vibe code a marketplace or a directory for random off-the-wall niche wedding services.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: they rent out this donkey for $700 for a day.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Niche white-labelled vibe-coding app
ideas.one_liner: White-label Lovable/Replit for one niche (e.g. 'Lovable for video games') with guided prompts and an upsell to human engineers for the last 10-20%.
ideas.customer: Kids and adults wanting to build games
ideas.problem: Non-coders want to build their own game
ideas.offer: Niche vibe-coding wrapper with scaffolding prompts

pricing.model: Cheap subscription plus premium human help

ideas.delivery: White-labelled vibe-coding platform; engineers for upsell.
risks: Underlying platforms add the niche themselves

quotes.text: I really like the idea of white labeling a vibe coding service like lovable or replet.

tactics.name: Shopify order-confirmation cold outreach
steps: Create a Shopify store (trial)
Build a CSV of dummy orders with target emails and a product name that is your pitch (e.g. 'Outsource stump grinding')
Import orders, mark as paid, trigger confirmation emails that land in the primary inbox
Include a tailored message and quote link
If shut down, open a new account

quote.text: Shopify order confirmation emails almost always land in the primary inbox.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Directory-to-agency funnel
steps: Pick a high-ticket, high-trust vertical not saturated by marketers (healthcare, CPAs, lawyers)
Build a directory of all businesses with AI
Cold email each: you're listed, want to rank higher?
Upsell premium placement then PPC/SEO agency services
Build ~10 directories expecting 2-3 winners

tactics.name: Permissionless directory then charge
steps: Scrape niche vendors into a directory in one city
Send them free leads
Return later: pay (e.g. $100-250/month) for placement or ads, or be removed

quote.text: Hey, you're getting leads from my website. I'm going to charge you now or I'm going to take you off the website.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Port features from mature industries to sub-industries
steps: Find a feature new in a big industry (touchless car rental pickup)
Apply it as a service to a smaller adjacent industry (boat, ATV, kayak rentals)
Sell it to those companies as SaaS

quote.text: find an established industry like car rentals, been around forever. Look at the features and the offerings that are just now starting to come out
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Copy a proven subscription in a new genre
steps: Take The Flower Letters model
Pick other top Amazon fiction categories for women (post-apocalyptic, space opera, Renaissance Italy)
Launch one or several series
Use paid Meta ads the incumbent isn't using

tactics.name: Roll up Facebook groups for distribution
steps: Buy niche Facebook groups (as done for Texas Snacks with a Buc-ee's group)
Merge them to build a list
Sell a subscription to members

quote.text: You went and bought a BIES Facebook group. You could go and probably buy some chess groups, roll them up, merge them together.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: The Shopify fake-order outreach hack risks account termination and abuses platform trust; in the UK it would also breach PECR when sent to individuals or sole traders without consent, and fake 'paid order' emails could be misleading.

quote.text: How quickly do you get shut down by Shopify?
quote.speaker: Nick

warnings.warning: Directories monetised only by banner ads earn little; you need volume or B2B monetisation.

quote.text: most directories monetized by just banner ads, which is like the lowest form of monetization.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Home services are over-saturated with marketers; look elsewhere for directory/agency plays.

quote.text: I think home services are kind of overly saturated.
quote.speaker: Nick

warnings.warning: Directories take time to build SEO traction; don't expect immediate results.
High gross margins can hide heavy customer acquisition spend below the line.
Vibe-coding gets you 80-90% of the way; the last 10-20% (integrations, payments, security) needs engineers.

quote.text: it's really easy to build the first 80% or 90%. It's that last 10 or 20% that you can vibe code to
quote.speaker: Nick

lessons.lesson: Most valuable local knowledge isn't on the internet, which protects offline businesses from AI.

quote.text: Most of everything is not on the internet, believe it or not.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Location, domain and history create moats that let destination businesses charge huge premiums.

quote.text: This is what a legal monopoly looks like. This is what a moat looks like.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Zig while others zag: slow, analog experiences can win in an instant-gratification world.
Serialised products have very low churn because customers want to know how the story ends.
A small B2B audience can be worth more than a large consumer audience for directories.

quote.text: I'd much rather have the latter
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Low USPS bulk postage is an underappreciated subsidy for mail-based businesses.

quote.text: one of the largest subsidies, marketing subsidies that nobody talks about is the United States Postal Service.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Companies that offload logistics (retailers not wanting to move hot tubs) create service niches.
Start a marketplace as a directory in one local market, doing things that don't scale, before expanding.

quote.text: I would start small. I would go in one market, do something that doesn't scale, see how it works, and then scale it.
quote.speaker: Nick

lessons.lesson: AI grows the pie and gives individuals the power institutions used to have; good content will stand out more.
An incumbent with no paid ads leaves room for a well-funded copycat to grow the category.

evidence_quality.rationale: Brainstorm podcast; figures are second-hand (USPS blog, observed prices, guest anecdotes) and several are back-of-envelope estimates (Flower Letters profit).
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: GoHighLevel sponsor read; Chris promotes TK Owners ($99/month) and his newsletter; Nick promotes One Life Tale.
